standard_prerequisites.name: Dependent product of contractible types
standard_prerequisites.statement: prd x:A P(x) is contractible when each P(x) is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion of the theorem.

standard_prerequisites.name: Retract
standard_prerequisites.statement: X is a retract of Y when there are maps in both directions whose composite is homotopic to the identity on X.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof exhibits prd x:A P(x) as a retract of the fiber of alpha at the identity, whence contractibility transfers.

standard_prerequisites.name: Uniqueness principle for dependent function types
standard_prerequisites.statement: A dependent function is equal to its own eta-expansion.
standard_prerequisites.use: It identifies psi(varphi(f)) with f at source line 972.

core_obligations: Define varphi : (prd x:A P(x)) -> hfiber alpha id by varphi(f) := (lam x (x, f(x)), refl id) (source lines 964-968).
Define psi : hfiber alpha id -> prd x:A P(x) by psi(g,p) := lam x, trans (happly(p,x)) (proj2 (g x)) (source lines 969-971).

Show that psi(varphi(f)) = lam x, f(x), which is f by the uniqueness principle for dependent function types, so the composite is homotopic to the identity and the product is a retract of the fiber (source line 972).

Conclude that the product is contractible, since the fiber of alpha at the identity is contractible by the retained corollary and contractibility is preserved by retracts, which is the weak function extensionality principle (source lines 960-961 and 973).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the two maps exhibiting the product as a retract of the fiber.
Compute the composite by the uniqueness principle and conclude contractibility.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled theorem `uatowfe` at source lines 957-961: in a univalent universe, if P is a family of contractible types then the dependent product of P is a retract of the fiber of alpha at the identity, hence is contractible, so univalence implies weak function extensionality. The author's proof (source lines 963-973) constructs the retraction explicitly: varphi packages a dependent function as a point of the fiber together with a reflexivity path (lines 966-967), psi evaluates the transported second component pointwise (lines 969-970), and the composite is then identified with the identity by the uniqueness principle for dependent function types (line 972). The conclusion is reached only through the retained corollary that names the map alpha and the fact that contractibility is inherited by retracts. The statement mentions neither the two maps nor the retraction computation.
